title: Portability T5c: bootstrap script and stable project key
problem: Persistent state lives under ~/.claude/projects/<key>/, where <key> is currently derived from cwd (e.g. 'D--Professional-claude-apiary'). Different machines produce different keys for the same repo, so notes, learnings, memory, and budgeter logs do not follow the repo across machines. There is also no idempotent bootstrap step — new clones require manual directory creation and auto-startup flag seeding.
description:
Third phase of the portability epic (T5), follows T5a (paths/interpreter) and T5b (shell hygiene).

DEPENDENCY: Do not start until T5b's pipeline/* branch is merged to master.

Scope of work:
1. scripts/bootstrap.py (new, idempotent):
   - Creates ~/.claude/projects/<key>/ if missing
   - Seeds empty notes.jsonl, learnings.jsonl
   - Creates memory/ directory with empty MEMORY.md if missing
   - Seeds auto-startup-enabled flag at ~/.claude/auto-startup-enabled if missing (default: on)
   - Verifies Python version meets the min declared in T5a
   - Verifies requirements.txt deps are installed; prints 'pip install -r requirements.txt' hint if not
   - Safe to run multiple times — never clobbers existing data
2. Stable project key derivation:
   - Option A: a .claude-project-key file at repo root holding a stable string (checked into git)
   - Option B: hash of the git remote URL (computed at runtime)
   - Pick one and implement it in whatever module currently derives the key (likely scribe or a shared helper). Decision rationale must be recorded in the spec.
   - The new key MUST produce a path that is filesystem-safe on Windows, macOS, and Linux (no colons, no leading dots that hide on Unix, etc.)
3. One-time migration for the CURRENT machine:
   - scripts/migrate_project_key.py: detects the old cwd-derived key (D--Professional-claude-apiary) and the new stable key, moves the directory, updates any scribe internal pointers, prints a summary.
   - Idempotent: refuses to run if old dir doesn't exist; refuses to clobber if new dir already populated.
   - Document the migration in the PR description.
4. Update any code that currently reads the cwd-derived key to read the new stable key instead.

Definition of done:
- scripts/bootstrap.py exists, is idempotent, works on a fresh ~/.claude
- Project key is stable across machines and a decision document exists in the spec
- Current machine migrated (~/.claude/projects/<new-key>/ now holds notes, learnings, memory)
- scribe and any other consumers read the new key
- No regression: scribe/notes.py list still returns the same notes after migration

Out of scope (deferred): PORTABILITY.md, migration guide document, fresh-VM acceptance test (all T5d).
scope: scripts/bootstrap.py (new), scripts/migrate_project_key.py (new), scribe/ project-key derivation, any other module that reads the project key, .claude-project-key (new, if that option wins). Touches scribe state management — be careful not to corrupt existing notes/learnings.
context: Phase 3 of the portability epic split. Depends on T5b landing first. T5d (docs + fresh-VM validation) queued after.
